extracted.intended_audience: United States Indian Agents; Commissioner of Indian Affairs; reservation administrators and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: An annual field report from a U.S. Indian agent describing operations, problems, and recommendations across schooling, agriculture, policing, sanitation, allotments, and resource management on a reservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicious distribution of government livestock
rubrics_metrics.description: I have distributed the 600 cattle as judiciously as I could, assigning them to those, who, I thought, would take the best care of them, and to those the most worthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign government-supplied stock to individuals judged most likely to care for them and most deserving. Implicit anti-pattern: distributing indiscriminately or by favoritism that ignores ability to care for animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure reduction in horse-theft by relocation and policing
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the removal of the Indians to the Washita River, the raids of horse-thieves upon their stock have been less frequent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frequency of horse-theft reports as an outcome metric for relocation and police effectiveness; relocation nearer sources of enforcement reduces weekly theft occurrences.

rubrics_metrics.name: School capacity and parental interest as success indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Both buildings were filled to about their capacity, and the children have made fair progress in their studies. ... the parents have shown an interest in the school and have manifested an anxiety to have their children brought up in the white man's ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate schools by enrollment relative to capacity, pupil progress, and parental support. Positive signals include full buildings, observable progress, and parents' expressed desire to educate children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use salaried teachers instead of contract system
rubrics_metrics.description: I am glad the contract system has been abolished, and our schools are to be run under regular salaried teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer regular salaried teachers over contract systems for stability and better educational outcomes; contract-based teaching viewed as inferior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious organization and meeting-house provision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Wichitas and affiliated bands have quite an interesting church organization, consisting of about 70 members. During the past year they have built a very nice meeting-house...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support and note local church organizations and meeting-houses as indicators of community organization and moral/spiritual development; funding may be partly local/white-subscribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary monitoring and physician reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: There have been comparatively but few serious cases of sickness. I invite attention to accompanying report, marked 'C,' of the agency physician.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track serious sickness incidence and refer to physician reports for clinical detail; keep separate physician reports appended to the agent's annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian police organization and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Indian police force at this agency was organized October 1st, 1878, and numbers 1 captain, 1 lieutenant, 4 sergeants, and 22 privates. ... They have done as well as could be expected of them, considering that arms were not furnished by the government until a couple of months ago.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize a disciplined Indian police force with clear ranks; provide arms and training. Use police for law enforcement, removal of unauthorized grazers, messenger duties, recovering stray stock, and camp intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer freighting by Indians when reliable
rubrics_metrics.description: The freighting by the Indians has proved a perfect success, and I will do them the credit to say that during the freighting of the past fourteen months not a single case has been reported to me of a package being lost or being in the slightest way tampered with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure freighting success by loss/tampering statistics. If local freighting by Indians shows no losses, favor it over contractor systems; provide wagons and coordinate logistics as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment of Indians in agency labor roles
rubrics_metrics.description: I have had on my rolls, the past year, at one time as many as forty Indians as laborers, and many of them are very efficient and fill the places assigned them as well as whites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ Indians across saw-mill, butchering, hauling, quarrying, carpentry, herding and driving; evaluate by efficiency and reliability compared to white labor; regard employment as civilizing and enabling self-support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarantine and prompt treatment for Texas cattle fever
rubrics_metrics.description: The disease ... made its appearance among our domestic cattle. ... Accordingly ... resorted at once to spirits of turpentine in the form of an emulsion with thin starch, in the proportion of 4 ounces of turpentine to 32 ounces of thin starch. This was administered at one dose by drenching. It was repeated according to indications. ... Only one case proved fatal after the turpentine treatment was instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On detecting cattle fever: isolate newly introduced herds, hold them distant until disease disappears, and consider prompt treatment with turpentine emulsion (4 oz turpentine to 32 oz thin starch) by drenching, repeating as indicated. Prompt intervention and quarantine limit mortality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government farm as training/education resource
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government Farm comprises about 160 acres ... The labor on the farm has, except running the harvester, been done almost entirely by Indian employes. Our agricultural operations cannot as yet be called a success financially, but as an efficient educating force it deserves to stand high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the government farm primarily as an educational/training asset (teaching machine operation, threshing, grain care) rather than a pure profit center. Track both financial performance and training outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit squaw patches on government farm except limited gardens
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of permitting squaw patches in the government farm ... seems to me to be productive of much more harm than good, and will be entirely stopped save garden patches for families of employes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disallow informal individual claims ('squaw patches') on government farm to prevent loafers congregating; permit small garden patches only for employees' families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Band farms partnerships and equitable distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The band fields were worked in a partnership arrangement of their own. The produce was distributed according to the labor done by each family or person, equitably and satisfactorily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage band farms to operate as partnerships and distribute produce proportionally to labor contributed. For milling/grinding when individual profit arises, impose a toll (placed in government bin) rather than free grinding for all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain allotment records and field notes for land claims
rubrics_metrics.description: On examination, while I find provision made of an excellent and ample record book for allotments of land, there is not a single entry of allotment. The fact that there are not at this agency any field notes of the original survey is, perhaps, the reason why no entries have been made. ... We propose as soon as the field notes can be obtained to commence the rectification of this important matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep complete allotment record books and ensure field notes of original surveys are obtained and entered so residents have documented lines and ownership claims; remediate missing records promptly to avoid future disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper planting technique for fruit trees
rubrics_metrics.description: The investment in fruit trees seems to be almost an absolute failure ... owing to being simply heeled in, in masses, and not properly set out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant fruit stock properly (set out individually) instead of heeling-in masses; timing and proper setting affect survival and productivity; grape varieties (Concord) may be promising if properly handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with treaty education provisions and enforce attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: By treaty with the Pawnees ... each and every one of their children, between the ages of seven and eighteen years shall be kept constantly at school, for at least nine months in each year. A distinct penalty in the way of forfeiture is provided for those who fail, neglect, or refuse to so keep their children at school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize treaty obligations to provide school facilities and enforce attendance (7–18 years, nine months per year) with penalties for noncompliance. Consider day schools in each band with resident teachers to fulfill obligations more economically and effectively than limited boarding schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Day school model with resident teacher and practical instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The establishment of four district schools, one in each band, would seem most perfectly to fulfill all the conditions prescribed. A resident teacher could gather in all the children of suitable age of both sexes, have one session per day, and for the rest of the time be a local superintendent for the band, giving them instruction ... in agriculture, mechanics, and horticulture, and domestic management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement day schools located in each band with a resident teacher who provides classroom instruction plus practical training and local supervision; use day schools as feeders to industrial boarding schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervene against harmful marriage practices undermining education
rubrics_metrics.description: Their system of exchange of marriageable daughters for ponies ... The practice of marrying off girls at the early and tender age so frequently done is most injurious and reprehensible. ... I learn of three girls ... who have been withdrawn from school to be married, thus failing and refusing to comply with the treaty obligation to keep the children at school until eighteen years old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address cultural practices (early marriage, exchange of daughters for ponies) that remove girls from school and contravene treaty educational goals; consider urgent advice or mandate to curb such practices to protect education and demographic stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized block delivery for meat distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The recent order changing the mode of delivery to the block was one eminently fit to be made ... it will distribute more justly the coveted and much prized beef ... Now the same ticket presented at the block, as at the commissary, insures a more just and equal distribution. The selfish and unequal appropriation by the leaders is effectually checked where it existed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver beef and similar rations at a central block using the same ticketing system as the commissary to ensure equitable distribution and prevent leaders from appropriating disproportionate shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and terminate counterproductive contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cimarron lumber contract has proved a heavy and expensive arrangement for this agency. It really retarded our improvements ... The difficulty of getting hands to stay and do logging was great and vexatious. ... I felt it to be my duty to stop operations on the Cimarron and report the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor contractor performance (deliverables like shingles, timeliness, cost, labor availability, haul distances). Terminate or suspend contracts that retard improvements or prove uneconomical, and report facts to higher authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide appropriate local equipment (e.g., shingle machine) to speed improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: A good shingle machine just now would be a splendid missionary for us, in enabling us to cover the roofless houses, giving assurance of being able to finish when we began to build.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in locally appropriate machinery (shingle machine, mill parts) to enable completion of building projects and reduce dependence on distant contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain mill machinery and water supply for economic operation
rubrics_metrics.description: I found on my first examination of the mill that the burrs had been almost ruined by unskillful or reckless use. ... Our new boiler has lain idle for want of necessary parts; we have just received the necessary pieces to complete it, and just as soon as our water supply enables us to get two or three issues ahead we will have it in place and be able to do efficient and economical work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure mill equipment (burrs, boiler) is properly maintained and balanced; procure necessary parts promptly and secure water supply adequacy to sustain regular production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure and deepen wells; construct new public wells when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: All the wells for drinking water failed except two. ... work has been commenced to deepen the dry wells. Two have been completed, the others will be deepened in turn. A new well for public use will be completed as rapidly as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to failing wells by deepening existing wells and constructing new public wells. Investigate causes (e.g., agricultural draw on percolation) and prioritize water projects as public benefactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect public water sources from contamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency well was so badly befouled ... that we were compelled to put a cover and key on it, in order to preserve it fit for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure wells and public water sources with covers and locked access where necessary to prevent fouling, vandalism, and contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve housing, ventilation, clothing and nutrition to advance public health
rubrics_metrics.description: The steady increase in the number of comfortable dwellings cannot fail to tell in the general health ... The crowded unventilated mud lodge has contributed, without doubt, to the prevalence of pulmonary affections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote construction of comfortable, ventilated dwellings, adequate clothing, and sufficient food (potatoes, vegetables) as foundational public-health measures; monitor reductions in malnutrition-linked disease as outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use skilled agency physician to replace superstitious practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Our physician is well educated, intelligent, faithful, and kind. His skillful and correct course of management and treatment is steadily decreasing the confidence of the tribe in the superstitious and silly practices of the native doctors...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ qualified physicians whose consistent correct practice will shift community trust from harmful traditional practices to effective medical care; document physician-led outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diplomatic handling of inter-tribal grievances and counsel procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Osages invited us to a friendly council ... All the chiefs and principal men were there. The Osages failed to come to the counsel of their own asking. ... I am holding them in quiet, expecting the authorities to do justice in this matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize councils with agreed time and place; treat no-show or insincere invitations as breaches of protocol; manage aggrieved parties with constrained restraint while escalating to authorities for remedy.
